canonical_topic: Natural Gas Physical Properties and Transport Implications
definition: The physical characteristics of natural gas that make its transportation and storage fundamentally different from solid or liquid fuels.
core_idea: Natural gas has low energy density compared to solids and liquids, and methane specifically is less energy dense than other hydrocarbon gases like propane; combined with the extreme cryogenic temperature (-263°F) required to liquefy it, this makes tank-based distribution impractical and pipelines the standard transport method.
key_points: Gas contains substantially less energy per unit volume than solids or liquids
Methane is one of the least energy-dense hydrocarbon gases, less dense than propane
Liquefying natural gas requires supercold temperatures (-263°F), making liquid-form consumer distribution impractical
These constraints make pipeline transport the typical solution
relationships: Sets up the need for pipeline pressure dynamics and storage facilities
